# dsh-infini-goal
English | 简体中文

A plugin suite for DeepSeek Harness (DSH):
it takes the domain model, model tools, and UI shape of t

he official `dsh-goal`, but reworks
"automatic continuation" into an **endless goal with no round ca

p, paced by a minimum interval,
and configurable quiet windows**.

- **No maximum rounds**: a goal stays `active` until it is completed, paused, blocked, or cleared;
-

**Minimum trigger interval**: two automatic rounds start at least `minIntervalMs` apart, so an
empt

y loop cannot spin into rapid retries;
- **Quiet windows** (`quietWindows`): no automatic triggers i

nside the configured local time
ranges; human conversation and tool calls keep working as usual, and

automatic progress resumes
when the window ends. Use them for do-not-disturb, focus time, off-hours
, nights, or anything else.

## Features
| Capability | Description |
| Endless continuation | No `maxGoalRounds`; `roundsStarted` only grows, so a goal can run indefinit

ely |
| Minimum trigger interval | Each automatic round starts at least the configured duration afte
r the previous one (default 1 minute, minimum 1 second, maximum 30 days), specifically to suppress e

mpty loops |
| Quiet windows | Supports midnight crossing, ISO weekday filters, and IANA time zones;

no automatic rounds inside a window |
| Event sourcing | Every change is persisted as an ignorable
`plugin:infini-goal/change` Session plugin record with strict replay validation; goals can be resume

d and forked |
| Session projection | The `infiniGoal` projection syncs the current goal to the brow

ser, so the UI needs no custom Remote API |
| Model tools | `get_infini_goal` / `create_infini_goal`

/ `update_infini_goal` |
| Human command | `/infini-goal` — inspect status, configure pacing, pause

/resume without spending model rounds |
| Status-bar UI | InfiniGoalBar above the composer: phase, r

ounds, trigger pacing, quiet-window hint, pause/resume/clear |
| Permission model | Every change nee
ds human authorization or the current automatic round's authorization; the model cannot rewrite the

goal on its own (see Permission model) |
| Coexistence | Tool, command, and status-bar names do not
collide with the official `dsh-goal`; a companion bundle can also switch the official goal off |
## UI

The status bar sits above the composer, in the same slot as the official goal's GoalBar
(`conversati

Status-bar states (phase label on the left, objective and rounds in the middle, pacing row and
butto

(phase label on the left, objective and rounds in the middle, pacing row and
buttons on the right):
| Goal state | Status bar shows | Buttons |
| `active`, minimum interval elapsed since the last round | Auto-continuing · objective · Rounds: N

· `next round in mm:ss` (refreshed every second) | Pause / Clear |
| `active`, minimum interval not

reached yet | Auto-continuing · objective · Rounds: N · `min interval 1m` | Pause / Clear |
| `activ
e`, inside a quiet window | Auto-continuing · objective · Rounds: N · `quiet window · until HH:mm` |

Pause / Clear |
| `paused` / `blocked` | Paused / Blocked (blocked also shows the reason) · Rounds:

N; no pacing row | Resume / Clear |
| `complete` or no goal | Nothing rendered | — |

The buttons only dispatch `/infini-goal ...` commands; no custom Remote API is involved. Command
err
ors are shown inline in the status bar.
## Differences from the official dsh-goal
| Dimension | Official `dsh-goal` | This plugin |

| Round cap | `maxGoalRounds` (default 256) | No cap |
| Trigger throttling | None; resumes immediat

ely when idle | Minimum trigger interval + quiet windows |
| Activation model | In-process `armed`/`
disarmed`; needs a manual resume after restore or fork | Durable `phase`: continues after an app res
tart or session restore (configurable `autoContinueOnStart: false`, which persists the goal as pause

d at startup) |
| Tools / commands | `get_goal` / `create_goal` / `update_goal`, `/goal` | `*_infini

_goal`, `/infini-goal`; coexists with the official goal |
| Remote API | Typert Remote | Not needed:
the UI reads a Session projection and actions go through the `/infini-goal` command |
### Prerequisites
| Item | Requirement |

| DSH | `0.2.2-rc.1` (plugin / bundle packages declare `engines.dsh: >=0.2.2-rc.1 <0.3.0`) |
| Node.
js | ≥ 24.9 (only needed for local build / publish / E2E; installing the plugin from npm does not ne

ed Node on this machine) |
| pnpm | 12.x (CI pins `pnpm@12.16.1`) |
| Web UI | DSH desktop app or `d
sh web`; the status bar only renders in the Web UI |
## Known limitations

- **Single goal**: each Session has exactly one infini-goal at a time.
- **Resume means continue**:

`active` is durable, so the goal continues after a DSH restart or a
session restore; with `autoConti

nueOnStart: false` the driver **durably pauses** active goals at
startup / agent creation, the statu

s bar shows paused and can resume, and a human must run
`/infini-goal resume`.
- **Forks continue to

o**: a forked child session contains the goal history and keeps advancing by
default; `pause` first

if you do not want that.
- **UI actions go through commands**: status-bar buttons send `/infini-goal

...` commands; no custom
Typert Remote is introduced.
- **The countdown is computed locally**: the

status bar derives the pacing row from the projection
and local per-second computation, so second-le

vel display drift is possible; the actual trigger is
computed by the driver with the same `planTrigg

er`.
- **Compatibility**: plugin / bundle packages declare `engines.dsh: >=0.2.2-rc.1 <0.3.0`; the p

lugins
must be updated before DSH moves to 0.3.
- **Single-session semantics**: goals and rounds bel

ong to the current Session; the plugin offers no
cross-session sharing or aggregation of goals.
